Microsoft Fabric icons for architecture diagrams

A diagramming reference built from the official @fabric-msft/svg-icons package, pinned to 8.2.0 (published 29 Jun 2026), with a coverage matrix against the Fabric REST ItemType enum, usage rules, and per-icon copy and download. Everything on this page is inline; it works offline.

7Non-item
14Color marks

4Archived (recovered)
793SVGs embedded

Read this first

The GitHub zip is stale.

fabric-samples/docs-samples/Icons.zip contains 6.1.0 (26 Feb 2026). npm latest is 8.2.0 (29 Jun 2026). 8.x adds ontology, mirrored_catalog, mirrored_generic_storage, data_quality and the shortcut glyph family, and renames graph_model_instance to graph_model. Treat npm as the source of truth; the zip is a snapshot. Verified 2026-09-05 against the npm registry and the zip contents.

Coverage is incomplete and the package does not say so.

18 of the 52 REST ItemType values have no item icon in 8.2.0, including Activator (Reflex), SQL endpoint, GraphQL API, Airflow job, Warehouse snapshot, Digital Twin Builder, Map, Anomaly detector, Snowflake and Cosmos DB databases, and dbt job. Four of those (Activator, Digital Twin Builder and Flow, Event schema set) existed in 4.0.3 and were removed in later regenerations; archived copies are included below and labeled. See coverage for the fallback per gap.

Four families, four jobs

FamilyFilename suffixSizesJob on a diagram
Item_item20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64Nodes. One icon per Fabric item. Full-color, non-recolorable (embedded gradients).
Non-item_non-item20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64Containers and actions: workspace, folder, sample, add pipeline, import notebook. Use workspace as a group header, never as a node.
Color_color16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 48Workload and product marks (OneLake, Power BI, Purview, Copilot, Data Factory). Legend or lane header, once per diagram.
Regular / Filled_regular, _filled12 to 48, mostly 20Monochrome glyphs that inherit currentColor. Edge labels, badges on nodes (shortcut, RLS, Git), sub-item detail (Delta table, SQL endpoint). Recolorable via CSS color or a fill replacement.

This page filters the Regular and Filled sets to Fabric-specific glyphs (142 of 572 upstream). Generic UI glyphs (arrows, calendars, datatypes, vehicles) are excluded because they do not belong on an architecture diagram; the full set is on npm.

Diagram usage rules

Node size

Pick one item size per diagram and hold it. 32 px for dense system diagrams (20 or more nodes), 40 px for the standard client architecture slide, 48 or 64 px for a hero or executive slide with fewer than eight nodes. Item icons are redrawn per size, not scaled: the 20 px variant drops interior detail. Do not scale a 64 px file down to 20 px; use the 20 px file.

Glyphs are annotations, not nodes

A glyph (Regular or Filled) never stands alone as a box on the diagram. It rides on an edge (shortcut, Git sync), sits as a badge on a node (RLS lock on a semantic model, SQL endpoint on a lakehouse), or appears in a legend. This is what keeps the item vocabulary readable: every full-color square is a Fabric item, every monochrome mark is a property or relationship.

Regular vs Filled

Choose one weight for the whole diagram. Regular reads better at 20 px on white; Filled reads better on dark backgrounds and on colored lane fills. Mixing them signals a state difference to the reader, so only mix when you mean it (for example, Filled for the active path in a failover diagram).

Color marks are headers

OneLake, Power BI, Purview, and the workload marks belong in a lane header or a legend, once. A Power BI mark beside every report node is noise; the report item icon already carries the meaning.

Shortcut, mirror, and endpoint conventions

Draw a shortcut as a dashed edge with the table_shortcut or folder_shortcut glyph at the consuming end. Draw a mirrored source as the mirrored_generic_database item plus a text label for the source system; the pack has no source-specific mirror icons. Draw the SQL analytics endpoint as a database_sql badge on the Lakehouse, since it is not an independently created item even though it has an ItemType.

Preview and archived items

When a node uses an archived icon (Activator, Digital Twin Builder, Event schema set), add a legend note that the icon is from a prior package version. When an item is preview in the tenant, annotate the node with a text tag rather than a different icon; the pack has no preview badge.

Recoloring

Glyphs use fill="currentColor"; set color on the container or replace the attribute. Item, Non-item, and Color icons embed gradients and hard-coded fills; recoloring them breaks brand recognition and is not supported. If a monochrome item icon is required (print, grayscale), rasterize and desaturate; do not hand-edit the paths.

Tool-specific guidance

Tool behaviors below are Training-era, not re-verified on 2026-09-05. Test one icon in your target tool before committing to a workflow.

ToolHow to bring icons inWatch for
draw.io / diagrams.netDrag the SVG file onto the canvas, or Arrange, Insert, Image with the file. For a reusable library, build a custom library (File, New Library) from the SVGs and share the .xml.Gradient IDs are unique per file, so multiple icons coexist. The Edit Style dialog cannot recolor item icons; expected.
PowerPoint / WordInsert, Pictures, This Device, choose the SVG. Office renders SVG natively and can Convert to Shape for glyphs.Convert to Shape on item icons loses gradients. Keep item icons as pictures; convert only glyphs when you need to recolor.
VisioInsert, Pictures, choose SVG. Save frequently used icons as a stencil (.vssx) so they carry connection points.Add connection points after import; imported SVGs have none.
ExcalidrawDrag and drop the SVG; it embeds as an image element. Group icon plus label before duplicating.Exported PNG/SVG re-embeds the icon, so file size grows per instance.
MermaidNo native SVG node icon support. Use HTML labels with an <img> data URI when the renderer allows HTML, or keep Mermaid for logic and re-draw the presentation view elsewhere.GitHub and most docs renderers strip HTML labels.
Markdown, HTML, docs sitesReference the SVG file or paste the data URI copied from this page. Set explicit width and height.Some static-site sanitizers strip inline SVG with <defs>; a data-URI <img> survives.
React / TypeScriptimport { Lakehouse32Item } from "@fabric-msft/svg-icons". Tree-shaken since 6.0.1; 8.0.0 adds an exports map for deep and SVG subpath imports.Names follow PascalCase(base) + size + Style; the 8.x graph icons have no style suffix (GraphModel32).
 
# Pin the version; the set changes monthly
npm install @fabric-msft/svg-icons@8.2.0

# Pull the raw SVGs without a build
npm pack @fabric-msft/svg-icons@8.2.0 && tar -xzf fabric-msft-svg-icons-8.2.0.tgz
ls package/svg | grep _item.svg

Package notes and provenance

Published versions

Verified against the npm registry on 2026-09-05. Not every changelog entry was published: 4.0.4, 5.0.0, 6.0.0, 6.0.1, 7.0.2 and 8.0.2 appear in CHANGELOG.md but have no tarball. Anything those entries claim to add (Audience, User-assigned identity, Activator rename) is not obtainable from npm. Published: 6.1.0 (26 Feb 2026), 7.0.0 (25 Mar), 7.0.1 (20 Apr), 8.0.0 (14 May), 8.0.1 (19 May), 8.1.0 (17 Jun), 8.2.0 (29 Jun 2026).

Delta: 6.1.0 zip to 8.2.0

Added item icons: ontology, mirrored_catalog, mirrored_generic_storage, data_quality. Renamed: graph_model_instance to graph_model, graph_model_instance_queryset to graph_queryset (both now without _item suffix). Added glyphs: table_shortcut, folder_shortcut, folder_search_shortcut, table_kql_shortcut, table_lightning_shortcut, table_triangle_shortcut, table_column_double_chevron_link and _shortcut, diagram_branch_shortcut, geometry_collection, polygon, line_squiggle, search_pulse, search_pulse_add, vehicle_car_multiple. No PNGs ship in 8.x; the zip's dist/png folder (29 MB) has no 8.x equivalent.

Archived icons

Four item icons were recovered from @fabric-msft/svg-icons@4.0.3 (published 16 Apr 2025) because their ItemType values are still current: reflex (Activator), digital_twin_builder, digital_twin_builder_flow, event_schema_set. Their rendering style predates the 6.0.0 regeneration and may differ slightly from the rest of the set. Filenames on this page use the _archived suffix so they are never confused with current upstream assets.

License

The icon package is MIT licensed, Copyright (c) 2025 Microsoft Corporation, per the LICENSE file shipped in the package. MIT permits use, modification, and redistribution with the copyright and permission notice retained. The package README describes the icons as intended for Fabric platform extension development; using them in architecture documentation is within the MIT grant. Microsoft trademark and brand guidelines still govern how the marks (Fabric, OneLake, Power BI, Purview, Copilot) may be presented; that is a separate question from the code license and is not addressed here.

Suggested attribution line for decks and docs: "Icons: @fabric-msft/svg-icons 8.2.0, MIT, Microsoft Corporation."
